To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an expression and purification protocol for the wild type human G protein α subunit hGα(i)1 that produces milligrams of highly pure protein and is suitable for NMR spectroscopy.

we have successfully developed an expression, purification and NMR characterization protocol for wild-type, isotopically-labeled hGα(i) that can be used for detailed investigations into the dynamics of Gα proteins and their interactions with RGS and other partners.

we have successfully developed and optimized a protocol for the expression, purification and NMR characterization of hGαi1, a key component of the heterotrimeric guanine nucleotide-binding protein (G protein) signaling system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a robust protocol for the production of isotopically enriched hGα(i2) that is suitable for NMR spectroscopy.
the development of protocols for the expression, purification and characterization of isotopical labeled Gα(i) subunit for N-terminal and backbone NMR studies.
developing a detailed understanding of the molecular mechanisms of RGS/Gα protein interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protocol described here is an excellent starting point for the preparation of isotopically enriched hGα(i) proteins for NMR studies of their dynamics and interactions.
the methods described in this paper provide a useful and efficient approach to preparing isotopically labeled hGα(i2) for NMR spectroscopy.

we successfully prepared and characterized isotopically labeled human wild-type Gα(i1), a critical component of heterotrimeric signaling pathways, which will allow for the study of the intramolecular dynamics of the protein in its apo and complexed states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully prepared isotopically labeled hGα(i) proteins in milligram quantities, and that we have optimized their NMR spectra by truncating the N-terminus.
we have developed a method to prepare milligram quantities of isotopicaly-labeled hGα(i) for NMR studies, which can be used to investigate protein dynamics in RGS/G protein complexes.
we have successfully developed an efficient protocol for the preparation of milligram quantities of isotopely labeled, highly active hGα(i).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a SUMO fusion expression system, a bacterial expression host strain that produces rare amino acids, supplementation of minimal media with small amounts of isotopically enriched rich media, and a lowered induction temperatures can be used to prepare milligram quantities of isotopical labeled Gα proteins for NMR studies.
it is possible to obtain high levels of expression of isotopically-labeled Gα subunits in E. coli and obtain good quality NMR spectra at near physiological temperatures.
the SUMO fusion system can be used successfully to prepare isotopically labeled hGα(i) subunits for NMR studies.
